subject: Usage escrow and stepwise rebate construct — NovaHealth
body:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lim <sarah.lim@novahealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Usage escrow and stepwise rebate construct — NovaHealth

Hi Sarah,

Thanks again for the time this morning. Per our discussion, attached is a short proposal and an XLSX with three stepwise rate scenarios:
- Scenario A: Conservative breakpoints (higher marginal discounts at larger tiers)
- Scenario B: Accelerated ramp (front-loaded credits + smaller marginal drops)
- Scenario C: Escrow-backed performance corridor (partial refund tied to latency/availability SLOs)

High-level ask from NovaHealth: predictable per-token economics for a hosted API usage profile (mixed chat + embeddings), with protection if we miss throughput targets early in the commit. We sketched an escrow + stepwise rebate as a compromise between a large prepay and a pure blended discount.

Attachment: Redwood_NovaHealth_Proposal_v1.pdf (proposal stub)
Attachment: rate_scenarios_breakpoints.xlsx (workbook with modelled monthly tokens, marginal vs blended math)

If this looks directionally correct I can: 1) model your actual monthly token estimates into Scenario C; 2) produce a v2 with an escrow schedule and proposed SLOs that trigger partial release/return of escrow.

Thanks,
Dylan

--
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
D: +1 415-555-0172

----------------------------------------

From: Sarah Lim <sarah.lim@novahealth.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@novahealth.com
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Usage escrow and stepwise rebate construct — NovaHealth

Dylan,

Thanks for sending this over. A few quick clarifying questions from our side:
1) Escrow mechanics — who holds the escrow? Do you have a suggested escrow agent or do we escrow into a Redwood-controlled account with contractual triggers?
2) Performance corridor — what SLOs are you willing to tie refunds to (p99 latency, availability %, token loss)? Can we see concrete examples of refund math for a missed SLO?
3) Marginal vs blended — procurement prefers a blended effective rate for budgeting, but the engineering team likes the marginal ladder because it exposes incentives. Can you provide one worked example showing how the effective blended rate evolves across three months of growth?

Procurement also asked for a simple table showing: committed monthly tokens, marginal rate at each breakpoint, blended effective rate, and any clawback windows.

Appreciate it — we’re aiming for a decision cycle next week if the numbers are clean.

Best,
Sarah
Sarah Lim
Head of Product Integrations, NovaHealth

----------------------------------------

On Thu, Apr 22, 2027 at 15:30 Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Sarah —
>
> Appreciate the clear list. Quick answers and I'll follow up with the updated workbook and a sample escrow term sheet: 
>
> 1) Escrow mechanics: our legal prefers a third-party escrow agent for larger deals; for pilot-size deals we can structure an escrow account managed by NovaHealth's bank with a joint-release clause (both parties sign to release) or a unilateral release-to-customer if SLOs are not met. I'll attach a short term sheet in v2.
>
> 2) SLO triggers: we propose a two-tier SLO for the corridor: 
>   - Availability: 99.9% monthly uptime for the dedicated route (exclusions: scheduled maintenance, force majeure)
>   - Latency: p99 <= 1.2s for inference under normal batch sizing and concurrency policy
> Refund math example (Scenario C):
>   - Committed monthly tokens: 1,000,000
>   - Escrow deposit: $50,000 (applies to q1 of commitment)
>   - If availability falls between 99.5% and 99.9% in a month, release 50% of escrow back to customer as a credit applied to that month. If availability <99.5%, refund 100% of that month's pro-rated escrow amount to customer as credit.
>   - Latency breach: single month p99 > 1.2s triggers a capped rebate equal to 10% of estimated token spend for that month (up to escrow balance).
>
> 3) Marginal vs blended worked example (brief):
>   - Month 1 usage: 500k tokens. Marginal ladder applies: 0-250k @ $0.0009, 250k-500k @ $0.0007 => blended = ((250k*0.0009)+(250k*0.0007))/500k = $0.0008 per token
>   - Month 2 usage: 1.2M tokens. Marginal rates drop on incremental tokens; blended effective rate across both months is weighted by token volumes (we'll show month-by-month in the workbook).
>
> Im attaching a quick v2 with the sample math and a draft escrow term sheet. Ill also prepare a single-page table for procurement showing committed monthly token bands, marginal rate, and the blended effective rate for budget review.
>
> Attachments: Redwood_NovaHealth_Proposal_v2.pdf, rate_scenarios_breakpoints.xlsx
>
> Cheers,
> Dylan

----------------------------------------

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Usage escrow and stepwise rebate construct — NovaHealth

Looping in Sales Ops notes and a suggested guardrail:

On pricing mechanics — recommend we: 
- Cap total escrow exposure to 25% of estimated first-quarter committed spend to limit balance-sheet risk.
- Allow a 30-day reconciliation window after quarter-end for usage true-up (clawbacks applied only within that window).
- Define SLO measurement: we should publish the metric definitions and the telemetry endpoints we will provide NovaHealth for independent verification.

On the marginal vs blended ask — include in v2 a one-line: "For budgeting, Redwood will publish an expected blended effective rate each month given the committed plan. For invoicing, marginal rates apply to consumed tokens, with monthly true-up to produce an effective blended outcome." That tends to satisfy procurement while keeping the marginal incentive alignment.

Also, suggest we propose a short pilot (2 months) with reduced escrow ($10k) to validate telemetry and SLO measurement before full quarter commit.

Ben
Head of Sales Ops

----------------------------------------

From: Sarah Lim <sarah.lim@novahealth.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, procurement@novahealth.com
Cc: Mike Connor (CFO) <mike.connor@novahealth.com>
Date: Sat, 24 Apr 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Usage escrow and stepwise rebate construct — NovaHealth

Dylan / Ben,

This all looks reasonable and much clearer. Procurement is comfortable with the cap (25% Q1 exposure) and the 30-day reconciliation window. Engineering liked the telemetry endpoints and the SLO definitions Ben suggested.

We are fine starting with a 2-month pilot: escrow $10,000, target committed tokens month 1 = 500k, month 2 = 1.0M. If telemetry verification passes, we will execute the full quarter commit and move escrow to $50,000.

Please send the DocuSign for the pilot SOW and the pilot invoice/escrow instructions. I'll loop in our legal if we need further term tweaks.

Thanks — Sarah

Attachment references: pilot_SOW_stub.pdf (will sign via DocuSign)

--
Sarah Lim
Head of Product Integrations, NovaHealth
